sites.name: Apollo 11 Eagle
sites.notes: LROC-measured LM position, uncertainty 0.3 m (Wagner et al. 2016, Icarus; the LROC table gives east longitude 0-360). Touchdown 20:17:40 UT per NASA NSSDCA (https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=1969-059C), truncated to the minute.

sites.name: Apollo 12 Intrepid
sites.notes: LROC-measured LM position, uncertainty 2.2 m (table longitude 336.5781 east, converted). NSSDC lists the same point as -23.4219. Touchdown 06:54:35 UT per NASA NSSDCA (https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/lunar/apollo12info.html), truncated to the minute.

sites.name: Apollo 14 Antares
sites.notes: LROC-measured LM position, uncertainty 0.4 m (table longitude 342.52806 east, converted). Touchdown 09:18:11 UT per NASA NSSDCA (https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/lunar/apollo14info.html), truncated to the minute.

sites.name: Apollo 15 Falcon
sites.notes: LROC-measured LM position, uncertainty 1.0 m. Touchdown 22:16:29 UT per NASA NSSDCA (https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=1971-063C), truncated to the minute.

sites.name: Apollo 16 Orion
sites.notes: LROC-measured LM position, uncertainty 3.0 m. Touchdown 02:23:35 UT per NASA NSSDCA (https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/lunar/apollo16info.html), truncated to the minute.

sites.name: Apollo 17 Challenger
sites.notes: LROC-measured LM position, uncertainty 3.5 m. Touchdown 19:54:57 UT per NASA NSSDCA (https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/lunar/apollo17info.html), truncated to the minute.

sites.name: IM-1 Odysseus
sites.notes: Position from NASA's caption of the LRO LROC image of the lander taken 24 Feb 2024; the page states no uncertainty. Near Malapert A, about 1.5 km from the intended target. Touchdown 6:24 p.m. EST (23:24 UTC) per the same NASA page.
sites.outcome: Landed and came to rest in a degraded crater on a 12 degree slope

sites.name: IM-2 Athena
sites.notes: Position as published on the LROC page for the post-landing oblique image (near the centre of Mons Mouton); the page states no uncertainty. NASA gives touchdown as approximately 11:30 a.m. CST on 6 March 2025 (about 17:30 UTC; the time is approximate, not to the minute) at https://www.nasa.gov/blogs/missions/2025/03/06/intuitive-machines-mission-lands-near-south-pole-carrying-nasa-science/ .
sites.outcome: Landed on its side, more than 400 m from the intended site; batteries depleted within a day

sites.name: Blue Ghost Mission 1
sites.notes: Position as published on the LROC page for the lander image (elevation -3650 m); no uncertainty stated. Near Mons Latreille in Mare Crisium. Touchdown 3:34 a.m. EST on 2 March 2025 (08:34 UTC) per NASA's release https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/touchdown-carrying-nasa-science-fireflys-blue-ghost-lands-on-moon/ .

sites.name: IM-3 Reiner Gamma (planned)
sites.notes: Planned target region, not a landing: the Lunar Vertex science team's EGU 2024 abstract (Vines, Ho, Blewett et al.) gives the Reiner Gamma landing region as 7.585 N, 58.725 W, quoted to 3 decimals with no stated ellipse or uncertainty. Intuitive Machines flies this CLPS task order (CP-11) on a Nova-C lander. NASA's IM-3 page (https://www.nasa.gov/gallery/intuitive-machines-im-3/, updated 22 May 2026) names Reiner Gamma without coordinates and describes the mission in the future tense; not launched at the time of this check (15 Nov 2026), launch date not confirmed by NASA.

sites.name: Blue Ghost Mission 2 (planned, far side)
sites.notes: Planned target region, not a landing. Point is the Rashid-2 rover landing region on the north-eastern rim of Nassau F crater (23.82 S, 177.7 W; EPSC 2026 abstract EPSC2026-593, Flahaut et al.), which that abstract places on the Firefly Blue Ghost 2 mission. Firefly's own page (https://fireflyspace.com/missions/blue-ghost-mission-2/) lists the Mission 2 site as the far side near Nassau Crater with no coordinates, and the abstract does not state that this point is the lander's own target centre, so treat it as a region, quoted to 2 decimals with no stated ellipse. Not launched at the time of this check (15 Nov 2026); Firefly lists launch as no earlier than 2027.

sites.name: SLIM Moon Sniper
sites.notes: Position from NASA's caption of the LRO LROC image of the lander taken 24 Jan 2024; no uncertainty stated. Targeted a small crater (Shioli) on a slope. Touchdown 10:20 a.m. EST (15:20 UTC) on 19 Jan 2024 per the same NASA page.

sites.name: HAKUTO-R Mission 1 (ispace)
sites.notes: Commercial (ispace, Japan) lander that was aiming for Atlas crater. Point is the LROC-identified surface change near the nominal landing site, taken as the impact site, from the LROC page (47.581 N, 44.094 E; NAC imaging on 26 Apr 2023); the page states no uncertainty. Contact was lost at 12:40 p.m. EDT (16:40 UTC) on 25 Apr 2023 per the same page.
sites.outcome: Crashed during the landing attempt; no soft landing

sites.name: HAKUTO-R Mission 2 Resilience (ispace)
sites.notes: Commercial (ispace, Japan) lander that was targeting Mare Frigoris. Point is the LROC-measured impact site, listed as 60.4445 N, 355.4120 E (converted here to -4.588 east); the page states no uncertainty. Hard landing 5 June 2025 18:13 UTC per the same LROC page; NASA's LRO imaged the site on 11 June 2025 (https://www.nasa.gov/missions/lro/nasas-lro-views-ispace-hakuto-r-mission-2-moon-lander-impact-site).
sites.outcome: Crashed; hard landing, no soft touchdown

sites.name: Chandrayaan-3 Vikram (Statio Shiv Shakti)
sites.notes: Position from the LROC featured-image page (elevation 532 m); no uncertainty stated. The IAU gazetteer centre for Statio Shiv Shakti is -69.37, 32.32 (https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/16272); it agrees with the LROC value to 0.01 degrees. LROC value used. Landing date from ISRO (https://www.isro.gov.in/Chandrayaan3.html); time of day not published by primary source, so actual_landing_utc is date-only (T00:00Z).
sites.outcome: Landed; lander and rover operated for about one lunar day

sites.name: Chang'e 3
sites.notes: LROC-measured lander position, uncertainty 9.1 m (table longitude 340.4883 east, converted). CNSA states Chang'e-3 soft-landed at 9:11 p.m. on Saturday 14 Dec 2013 (https://www.cnsa.gov.cn/english/n6465652/n6465653/c6479578/content.html; the page does not label the zone, read as Beijing time, UTC+8, giving 13:11 UTC).

sites.name: Chang'e 4 (Statio Tianhe)
sites.notes: LROC-refined lander position, uncertainty 13 m (95% confidence). Touchdown 02:26 UTC on 3 Jan 2019 as stated on the same LROC page. Von Karman crater, South Pole-Aitken basin.
sites.outcome: Landed on the far side; Yutu-2 rover deployed

sites.name: Chang'e 5 (Statio Tianchuan)
sites.notes: LROC-computed lander position, estimated accuracy 20 m, elevation -2570 m (published longitude 308.0839 east, converted). Touchdown 10:11 EST (15:11 UTC) on 1 Dec 2020 as stated on the same LROC page.

sites.name: Chang'e 6
sites.notes: LROC-computed lander position, estimated horizontal accuracy 30 m (published longitude 206.0148 east, converted; elevation -5256 m). CNSA states touchdown at 6:23 a.m. Beijing time on 2 June 2024 (https://www.cnsa.gov.cn/english/n6465652/n6465653/c10541840/content.html), which is 22:23 UTC on 1 June, matching the LROC date. Apollo basin, inside South Pole-Aitken.

sites.name: Luna 16
sites.notes: LROC-measured lander position, uncertainty 3.7 m. Landing date not recorded in this catalogue.

sites.name: Luna 17 (Lunokhod 1 carrier)
sites.notes: LROC-measured lander position, uncertainty 0.5 m (table longitude 324.99837 east, converted). Landing date not recorded in this catalogue.

sites.name: Luna 21 (Lunokhod 2 carrier)
sites.notes: LROC-measured lander position, uncertainty 13.4 m. Landing date not recorded in this catalogue.

sites.name: Luna 24
sites.notes: LROC-measured lander position, uncertainty 3.7 m. Landing date not recorded in this catalogue.

sites.name: Shackleton rim at the connecting ridge junction
sites.notes: LROC-published point where the Shackleton-de Gerlache ridge meets the Shackleton crater rim (longitude 196.739 east, converted); no uncertainty stated. Shackleton is about 21 km across (IAU centre -89.67, 129.78, https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Feature/5450). An analysis point on the rim, not a landing target.

sites.name: Shackleton-de Gerlache connecting ridge
sites.notes: Midpoint of the bounds of the LROC NAC DTM of the connecting ridge (latitude -89.63 to -89.37, longitude 209.81 to 239.10 east, converted). A representative point on the ridge, not a measured landing position. The ridge is about 12-14 km long per https://lroc.im-ldi.com/images/1247 .

sites.name: Malapert Massif
sites.notes: LROC states that the relatively flat area at 86 S, 0 E is the heart of the candidate landing region on the massif. The LROC NAC mosaic centre for the same region is -86.0, 0.3 (see artemis3-malapert-massif). Representative point only.

sites.name: Mons Mouton
sites.notes: Centre of the LROC NAC combined mosaic of the Mons Mouton plateau (product NAC_ROI_MOUTNPLTLO1; centre -84.3, 30.6; mosaic extent latitude -85.76 to -82.85, longitude 15.49 to 46.61 east). The same point is used for artemis3-mons-mouton-plateau, which represents the Artemis candidate region; this entry is the general mountain analysis point and is not a measured landing position. IM-2 landed on the plateau at -84.7906, 29.1957 (see im-2). Representative point only.

sites.name: Artemis crewed landing candidate: Peak near Cabeus B
sites.notes: NASA's October 2024 list of nine candidate regions is still the current set: NASA's Artemis IV page (updated 16 Mar 2026, https://www.nasa.gov/mission/artemis-iv/) lists nine regions near the south pole. Artemis III is now a 2027 low Earth orbit test (NASA, 27 Feb 2026, https://www.nasa.gov/directorates/esdmd/nasa-strengthens-artemis-adds-mission-refines-overall-architecture/); the first crewed landing is planned for Artemis IV, early 2028. Checked 14 Nov 2026. NASA publishes no region coordinates; this is a representative point within a region of about 15 x 15 km. Point is the centre of the LROC NAC low-Sun mosaic for this region, encoded in product id P836S2912 (83.6 S, 291.2 E, converted).

Checked 14 Nov 2026. NASA publishes no region coordinates; this is a representative point within a region of about 15 x 15 km. Point is the centre of the LROC NAC low-Sun mosaic for this region (product NAC_ROI_HAWORTH_LOB_P867S3363: 86.7 S, 336.3 E, converted).

sites.name: Artemis crewed landing candidate: Malapert Massif
sites.notes: NASA's October 2024 list of nine candidate regions is still the current set: NASA's Artemis IV page (updated 16 Mar 2026, https://www.nasa.gov/mission/artemis-iv/) lists nine regions near the south pole. Artemis III is now a 2027 low Earth orbit test (NASA, 27 Feb 2026, https://www.nasa.gov/directorates/esdmd/nasa-strengthens-artemis-adds-mission-refines-overall-architecture/); the first crewed landing is planned for Artemis IV, early 2028. Checked 14 Nov 2026. NASA publishes no region coordinates; this is a representative point within a region of about 15 x 15 km. Point is the centre of the LROC NAC low-Sun mosaic for this region (product P860S0003). LROC's own prose point for the region heart is 86 S, 0 E (https://lroc.im-ldi.com/images/1294).

sites.name: Artemis crewed landing candidate: Mons Mouton Plateau
sites.notes: NASA's October 2024 list of nine candidate regions is still the current set: NASA's Artemis IV page (updated 16 Mar 2026, https://www.nasa.gov/mission/artemis-iv/) lists nine regions near the south pole. Artemis III is now a 2027 low Earth orbit test (NASA, 27 Feb 2026, https://www.nasa.gov/directorates/esdmd/nasa-strengthens-artemis-adds-mission-refines-overall-architecture/); the first crewed landing is planned for Artemis IV, early 2028. Checked 14 Nov 2026. NASA publishes no region coordinates; this is a representative point within a region of about 15 x 15 km. Point is the centre of the LROC NAC combined mosaic for the plateau; that mosaic covers a wider area than the region (latitude -85.76 to -82.85), so the centre is only a rough representative point.

sites.name: Artemis crewed landing candidate: Mons Mouton
sites.notes: NASA's October 2024 list of nine candidate regions is still the current set: NASA's Artemis IV page (updated 16 Mar 2026, https://www.nasa.gov/mission/artemis-iv/) lists nine regions near the south pole. Artemis III is now a 2027 low Earth orbit test (NASA, 27 Feb 2026, https://www.nasa.gov/directorates/esdmd/nasa-strengthens-artemis-adds-mission-refines-overall-architecture/); the first crewed landing is planned for Artemis IV, early 2028. Checked 14 Nov 2026. NASA publishes no region coordinates; this is a representative point within a region of about 15 x 15 km. Point is the IM-2 intended landing site, which LROC describes as the central portion of one of NASA's Artemis 3 potential landing regions (Mons Mouton).

sites.name: Artemis crewed landing candidate: Nobile Rim 2
sites.notes: NASA's October 2024 list of nine candidate regions is still the current set: NASA's Artemis IV page (updated 16 Mar 2026, https://www.nasa.gov/mission/artemis-iv/) lists nine regions near the south pole. Artemis III is now a 2027 low Earth orbit test (NASA, 27 Feb 2026, https://www.nasa.gov/directorates/esdmd/nasa-strengthens-artemis-adds-mission-refines-overall-architecture/); the first crewed landing is planned for Artemis IV, early 2028. Checked 14 Nov 2026. NASA publishes no region coordinates; this is a representative point within a region of about 15 x 15 km. Point is the centre of the LROC NAC low-Sun mosaic for this region (product P839S0587). A peer-reviewed multi-criteria study (Pena-Asensio et al., arXiv 2406.19863) gives its best point in the region as -84.20156, 60.69989, about 10 km from the mosaic centre and inside the mosaic extent; LROC centre used.
